chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: Indeed, Shaytan blows into the anus of the human being until it is made to seem to him that wind has come out from him; so his wudu (ablution) is not invalidated except by wind that he hears or whose smell he perceives.

key_terms.الشَّيْطَانَ: Shaytan, who causes deceptive misgivings and confusion
key_terms.رِيحٌ: wind, i.e. passing gas that affects ritual purity
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُ: his wudu (ablution), the state of ritual purity for salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَجِدُ رِيحَهَا: he perceives its smell, meaning he is certain by odor
key_terms.يَسْمَعُهَا: he hears it, meaning he is certain by sound
key_terms.يَنْفُخُ: blows, meaning he causes a sensation or illusion

ai.seo_question: Does doubt about passing wind invalidate wudu (ablution) in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding doubt in ritual purity. It teaches that mere suspicion does not invalidate wudu (ablution); rather, certainty is established only by hearing the sound or perceiving the smell of passing wind.
